sources.title: ESICM guidelines on circulatory shock and hemodynamic monitoring 2025 (ESICM; Monnet X, Messina A, Greco M, et al. Intensive Care Med)
Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026 (SCCM/ESICM; Prescott H, et al. Crit Care Med, doi:10.1097/CCM.0000000000007075)
2025 Concise Clinical Guidance: an ACC expert consensus statement on the evaluation and management of cardiogenic shock (ACC; Sinha SS, et al. J Am Coll Cardiol, doi:10.1016/j.jacc.2025.02.018)

q_shock.text: Features of shock? Low BP, or poor perfusion (slow capillary refill, mottling, low urine output, confusion, raised lactate). Low BP is not required.

q_tension.text: Tension pneumothorax suspected (unilateral absent air entry, rising airway pressure, sudden collapse on ventilator)?

q_anaph.text: Anaphylaxis suspected (recent drug/blood/contrast exposure plus rash, angioedema or bronchospasm)?

q_bleed.text: Bleeding or major fluid loss the likely cause?

answers.label: Trauma with brain injury (GCS 8 or less)
Severely reduced LV or RV function
Tamponade, or dilated RV with suspected PE

e_noshock.title: Shock not established: reassess
actions: Repeat perfusion checks at short intervals: capillary refill, skin temperature, mottling, urine output, mental state.
Measure lactate and repeat if raised.
Re-enter this pathway if perfusion worsens.
cautions: Normal BP does not exclude shock; hypoperfusion can occur without hypotension.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_tension.title: Suspected tension pneumothorax
actions: Decompress immediately per local procedure, then place a chest drain (standard practice, not from the cited guideline).
Do not delay for imaging if the patient is peri-arrest.
If ventilated: check tube position and ventilator settings while preparing.
cautions: Steps in this node are standard practice, not taken from the cited shock guidelines. Needs local-protocol confirmation.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_anaph.title: Suspected anaphylactic shock
actions: Switch to the local anaphylaxis protocol now.
Stop the suspected trigger (infusion, blood, drug).
Secure airway early if there is airway swelling.
cautions: No anaphylaxis guideline was reviewed for this draft, so no doses are given here. Use the local protocol.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_haem.title: Haemorrhagic shock (trauma, no brain injury)
actions: Stop the bleeding: surgery, interventional radiology or local haemostasis; call the surgical team.
Activate the local massive transfusion protocol if needed.
Until major bleeding is controlled, ESICM 2025 suggests an initial systolic target of 80-90 mmHg (MAP 50-60).
Arterial line when practical.
cautions: Lower BP target applies only while bleeding is uncontrolled and only without brain injury.
Blood product ratios and tranexamic acid: follow local trauma protocol (not covered by sources reviewed).
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_haem_tbi.title: Shock with traumatic brain injury
actions: Stop bleeding sources; fluid and blood product choice per local trauma protocol.
ESICM 2025: aim for an initial MAP of 80 mmHg or more when GCS is 8 or less.
Arterial line when practical.
cautions: Involve neurosurgery early (standard practice, not from the cited guideline).
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_hypovol.title: Hypovolaemic shock (non-traumatic)
actions: Treat the source: GI bleed (endoscopy, transfusion per local protocol) or ongoing losses (GI, renal, burns).
Give fluid in measured boluses and reassess after each one.
Use a dynamic test (passive leg raise, or end-expiratory occlusion if ventilated and not breathing spontaneously) before giving more.
Arterial line if not improving or vasopressor needed.
cautions: Echo early if response is poor: a second shock type may coexist.
Source-specific steps here are standard practice, not from the cited guideline.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_cardiogenic.title: Likely cardiogenic shock
actions: Go to the pathway: Cardiogenic shock.
12-lead ECG now; look for ST elevation or acute ischaemia.
Arterial line; avoid large fluid boluses until filling status is clear.
cautions: Sepsis with cardiac dysfunction can look similar: check for infection.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_obstructive.title: Likely obstructive shock
actions: Tamponade: urgent drainage; call cardiology/cardiac surgery.
Suspected massive PE: start the local PE / reperfusion pathway and call the senior.
Support BP while the cause is treated; reassess the RV on echo after each intervention.
cautions: No PE or tamponade guideline was reviewed for this draft: reperfusion choice and drug doses must come from the local protocol.
Cause-specific steps here are standard practice, not from the cited guideline.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_septic.title: Likely septic shock
actions: Go to the pathway: Sepsis and septic shock: initial resuscitation.
Antimicrobials immediately, ideally within 1 hour of recognition (SSC 2026).
Measure lactate; start crystalloid resuscitation.
cautions: Septic shock can include myocardial dysfunction: repeat echo if not improving.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_noecho.title: Shock type not yet known
actions: Treat the most likely cause while arranging echo as soon as possible (first-line test for shock type, ESICM 2025).
Use a dynamic fluid-responsiveness test before repeat fluid boluses.
Arterial line if not responding to initial therapy or a vasopressor is needed.
Serial perfusion checks: capillary refill, lactate, urine output.
cautions: Mixed shock is common; reassess the type if the response is poor.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_undiff.title: Distributive or unclear shock
actions: Look for other causes: adrenal crisis, drugs or toxins, spinal cord injury, liver failure, recent anaesthesia.
If not responding to initial therapy: monitor cardiac output / stroke volume (ESICM 2025) and repeat echo.
Arterial line; measure CVP if a central line is in place.
Senior review of the working diagnosis.
cautions: Keep infection on the list until excluded; if septic shock is possible, do not delay antimicrobials (SSC 2026).
The list of other causes is standard practice, not from the cited guideline.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.
